# Configure a Sentinel policy set with pre-written policies

@include 'beta/beta.mdx'

As organizations adopt Terraform across multi-cloud environments, enforcing consistent security and compliance controls remains a major challenge. The policy-as-code approach in HCP Terraform requires deep expertise to author and enforce policies effectively.  

HCP Terraform introduces a pre-written policy catalog that helps introduce best practices that secure infrastructure without writing or sourcing policies manually. 

This topic shows how to create a policy set for Sentinel. If you want to use the pre-written policies for Terraform policy refer to [Terraform policy set with pre-written policies](/terraform/cloud-docs/workspaces/policy-enforcement/manage-policy-sets/pre-written/terraform-policy-pre-written). 

## Create new policy set 

1. Sign in to [HCP Terraform](https://app.terraform.io/login) or Terraform Enterprise and navigate to your organization. 
1. Choose **Settings** from the sidebar, then **Policy sets**. 
1. Choose the **Pre-written policies** option. 
1. Select **Sentinel**.
1. From the table, select all policies you want to add to the policy set. 
  - Click on a policy name to view the policy details. 
  - Use the filter bar to search for specific policies. 
  - Select all required policies. 
1. Click on the **Next** button. 
1. Use the **...** button for each policy or the **Actions** dropdown to define the enforcement level for the selected policies. Available levels for Sentinel policy are: 
  - **Advisory**: Failed policies never interrupt the run. They provide information about policy check failures in the UI. 
  - **Mandatory**: Failed policies stop the run. Unless the set containing the policy is configured to [allow overrides](/terraform/cloud-docs/workspaces/policy-enforcement/manage-policy-sets#allow-policy-level-overrides), Terraform does not apply runs until a user fixes the issue that caused the failure. 
  
  Refer to [Policy enforcement levels](/terraform/cloud-docs/workspaces/policy-enforcement/manage-policy-sets#policy-enforcement-levels) for more information. 
1. Click on the **Next** button. 
1. Configure the policy set by adding: 
    - **Policy set name**: a unique name for the policy set. You can use any combination of letters, numbers, `-`, and `_`. A name is required. 
    - **Policy set description**: an optional description of the policy set behavior. 
    - **Scope of policies**: the scope the HCP Terraform applies the policies to. Refer to [Policy set scope](/terraform/cloud-docs/workspaces/policy-enforcement/manage-policy-sets/configure#policy-set-scope) for details. 
1. Click **Create policy set** to finish.
